A Memorable Culinary Experience with Standout Dishes
Jul 2026 • Solo
For the amuse-bouche, I particularly liked the corn pie tee. However, I didn’t quite understand why the tonburi tartlet was meant to be eaten second. The caviar flavor wasn’t emphasized enough, and I couldn’t really discern what direction the tartlet was going for. Despite this, I found the first and last bites flavorful and enjoyable.

The Hau Plum – Genmaicha and Watermelon – Eucheuma both showcased fresh ingredients. I particularly liked that the watermelon was served after the Wild Greens – Enokitake, as it was refreshing after the previous course. The greens themselves were a bit bland for me; I felt that the dish focused more on highlighting the natural taste of the greens rather than building layers of flavor around them. The watermelon, on the other hand, had a well-balanced combination of flavors.

My favorite dishes were the Black Garlic – Brioche, Rice Dumpling Cake – Crown Daisy, and Broken Rice – Trumpet Mushroom.

The brioche was insanely good. It was extremely soft and pillowy while still feeling incredibly light, and I could definitely taste the sweet potato. The black garlic pâté that came with it was delicious and savory, and I thought it paired perfectly with the root vegetables. This dish was just out-of-this-world good, which was unexpected for a bread and a pâté. The aroma was also wonderful. If this restaurant sold the brioche separately like a bakery, I would 100% buy it every day.

The rice dumpling cake was delicious as well. It was soft and flavorful, and the soup that came with it complemented the entire dish. The filling inside was also soft and tender. Everything worked together really well.

The broken rice was another standout. I honestly didn’t expect a mushroom to be able to stand in for the usual pork chop in cơm tấm. I have to commend them for choosing trumpet mushroom for this dish because I think they really did the ingredient justice. The soup served alongside it was light and hearty, and it reminded me of the classic soups I would get at Asian restaurants. The sauce was a little too sweet for me, but I appreciated that they made it thicker. For a dish served in such a small portion, I thought that was a smart choice because the sauce coated the rice and mushroom well without overwhelming them.

I didn’t particularly enjoy the Aubergine – Spring Onion, but not because I thought it was a bad dish. I’m simply not very comfortable with gooey textures.

The Soursop – Greengage dessert was also great. I really liked the contrasting textures, and it wasn’t overly sweet. I thought it was a creative and satisfying dessert.

The petit fours were not too overpowering, which made them a pleasant way to finish the meal. The non-alcoholic pairing was also nice, and I particularly liked the Kvass.

Service was top-notch. Although, as an introvert, I was overstimulated by everything.

Best Dining Experience in Ho Chi Minh City
Mar 2026 • Couples
If I could give Tales by Chapters more than five stars, I would. We traveled across the entire country and dined at multiple Michelin-recommended restaurants along the way, but none of them even came close to this. This is the true heart of fine dining in Ho Chi Minh City.
The food is creative, beautifully plated, and bursting with flavors that redefine what plant-based vietnamese cuisine can be. It’s a masterclass in culinary storytelling.
Beyond the food, the staff are incredibly kind and genuinely attentive; they make you feel like a guest of honor from the moment you walk in. If you are in Saigon, do not miss this. It was, hands down, the best food experience of our entire trip.
